Saṃyutta Nikāya 48.59 (SN 48.59, PTS SN v 235) 6. Sūkarakhatavagga First Discourse on Arising “Bhikkhus, when what exists, by what being present, does arising come to be? When what exists, by what being present, does aging-and-death come to be? “Venerable sir, our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One, guided by the Blessed One, and take recourse in the Blessed One. It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One himself would clarify the meaning of this statement. Having heard it from the Blessed One, the bhikkhus will remember it. “Then listen, bhikkhus, and attend closely; I will speak. “Yes, venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied. The Blessed One said this: “Bhikkhus, when there is birth, by the presence of birth, arising comes to be. When there is birth, by the presence of birth, aging-and-death comes to be. “Venerable sir, when what exists, by what being present, does birth come to be? When what exists, by what being present, does existence come to be? “Bhikkhus, when there is existence, by the presence of existence, birth comes to be. When there is existence, by the presence of existence, aging-and-death comes to be. “Venerable sir, when what exists, by what being present, does existence come to be? When what exists, by what being present, does clinging come to be? “Bhikkhus, when there is clinging, by the presence of clinging, existence comes to be. When there is clinging, by the presence of clinging, aging-and-death comes to be. “Venerable sir, when what exists, by what being present, does clinging come to be? When what exists, by what being present, does craving come to be? “Bhikkhus, when there is craving, by the presence of craving, clinging comes to be. When there is craving, by the presence of craving, aging-and-death comes to be. “Venerable sir, when what exists, by what being present, does craving come to be? When what exists, by what being present, does feeling come to be? “Bhikkhus, when there is feeling, by the presence of feeling, craving comes to be. When there is feeling, by the presence of feeling, aging-and-death comes to be. “Venerable sir, when what exists, by what being present, does feeling come to be? When what exists, by what being present, does contact come to be? “Bhikkhus, when there is contact, by the presence of contact, feeling comes to be. When there is contact, by the presence of contact, aging-and-death comes to be. “Venerable sir, when what exists, by what being present, does contact come to be? When what exists, by what being present, does the sixfold base come to be? “Bhikkhus, when there is the sixfold base, by the presence of the sixfold base, contact comes to be. When there is the sixfold base, by the presence of the sixfold base, aging-and-death comes to be. “Venerable sir, when what exists, by what being present, does the sixfold base come to be? When what exists, by what being present, do the name-and-form come to be? “Bhikkhus, when there is name-and-form, by the presence of name-and-form, the sixfold base comes to be. When there is name-and-form, by the presence of name-and-form, aging-and-death comes to be. “Venerable sir, when what exists, by what being present, do name-and-form come to be? When what exists, by what being present, does consciousness come to be? “Bhikkhus, when there is consciousness, by the presence of consciousness, name-and-form come to be. When there is consciousness, by the presence of consciousness, aging-and-death comes to be. “Venerable sir, when what exists, by what being present, does consciousness come to be? When what exists, by what being present, does name-and-form come to be? “Bhikkhus, when there is name-and-form, by the presence of name-and-form, consciousness comes to be. When there is name-and-form, by the presence of name-and-form, aging-and-death comes to be. “Bhikkhus, thus consciousness and name-and-form are mutually dependent, mutually supportive; they stand in mutual dependence. Just as two sheaves of reeds might lean against each other, so too, consciousness and name-and-form are mutually dependent, mutually supportive; they stand in mutual dependence. When one discerns, bhikkhus, that ‘with birth as condition, aging-and-death comes to be,’ one has directly known this.

When one discerns, bhikkhus, that ‘with existence as condition, birth comes to be… with clinging as condition, existence comes to be… with craving as condition, clinging comes to be… with feeling as condition, craving comes to be… with contact as condition, feeling comes to be… with the sixfold base as condition, contact comes to be… with name-and-form as condition, the sixfold base comes to be… with consciousness as condition, name-and-form comes to be,’ one has directly known this. When one discerns, bhikkhus, that ‘with name-and-form as condition, consciousness comes to be,’ one has directly known this. When one discerns, bhikkhus, that ‘with consciousness as condition, name-and-form comes to be,’ one has directly known this. When one discerns, bhikkhus, that ‘thus consciousness and name-and-form are mutually dependent, mutually supportive; they stand in mutual dependence,’ one has directly known this. When one discerns, bhikkhus, that ‘when there is no birth, by the cessation of birth, aging-and-death ceases’—having directly known this—one declares final knowledge: ‘Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus! “Venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this: “Bhikkhus, when what exists, by what being present, does birth come to be? … [as above] … Thus consciousness and name-and-form are mutually dependent, mutually supportive; they stand in mutual dependence. When one discerns, bhikkhus, that ‘with ignorance as condition, volitional formations come to be; with volitional formations as condition, consciousness; with consciousness as condition, name-and-form; with name-and-form as condition, the sixfold base; with the sixfold base as condition, contact; with contact as condition, feeling; with feeling as condition, craving; with craving as condition, clinging; with clinging as condition, existence; with existence as condition, birth; with birth as condition, aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair come to be. Such is the origin of this entire mass of suffering. When one discerns, bhikkhus, that ‘with ignorance as condition, volitional formations come to be… such is the origin of this entire mass of suffering,’ one has directly known this. When one discerns, bhikkhus, that ‘with the remainderless fading away and cessation of ignorance comes cessation of volitional formations; with the cessation of volitional formations, cessation of consciousness; with the cessation of consciousness, cessation of name-and-form; with the cessation of name-and-form, cessation of the sixfold base; with the cessation of the sixfold base, cessation of contact; with the cessation of contact, cessation of feeling; with the cessation of feeling, cessation of craving; with the cessation of craving, cessation of clinging; with the cessation of clinging, cessation of existence; with the cessation of existence, cessation of birth; with the cessation of birth, aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair cease. “Bhikkhus, there are these five higher fetters.
Which five?”
Sensual lust for the form realm, sensual lust for the formless realm, conceit, restlessness, and ignorance— these, monks,
are the five higher fetters. For the direct knowledge,
full understanding, destruction, and abandoning of these five higher fetters, monks, the five faculties are to be developed.
What are the five?
Here, monks, a monk develops the faculty of faith, which culminates in the removal of lust, the removal of hatred, and the removal of delusion.
